correctness.rationale: Independent uniform random rankings of top ties admit a threshold representation with one uniform latent variable per participant; conditioned on those, different unmatched-edge blocking events are independent, giving the exact product integral. The finite edge-subset expansion follows by termwise integration. Rooted-tree messages are affine in the parent threshold; induction proves the polynomial-time forest algorithm, with degree-controlled rational denominators. A rank-two integral kernel with eigenvalues (2±sqrt(7))/6 proves the path recurrence and exact cycle trace. A reproducible standard-library verifier matches independent local-permutation enumeration on 9016 graphs, forest messages on 3110 graphs, 21 paths and 19 cycles, plus an independently realizable 3x3 instance (10054/46656 stable). Those finite checks corroborate, not substitute for, the proof.

The 2019 compact-indifference theorem addresses one certain side rather than graph-sparse reciprocity, and the 2026 preprint abstract describes #P-hardness without supplying the exact forest polynomial integration or path/cycle spectra. The forest sufficient condition is independent of either side having certain preferences. Actual published-finding corpus and literature searches for the blocking graph formula, top-tie forest algorithms, path/cycle transfer matrices and eigenvalues located no result implying this pair of new statements. value.rationale: The motivating 2026 result makes unrestricted exact stability counting #P-hard, while sparse mutual possible-blocking competition is a natural observable market restriction. The result provides exact rational computation even when both sides have uncertain preferences, and gives explicit path/cycle probabilities with a sharp asymptotic exponent. This is a structural tractability and quantitative-probability result rather than a routine exercise or an arbitrary finite parameter slice. No downstream application or priority certification is claimed.
